text:
sasha: Quick thought — should we make the gateway emit a small "progress" signal to clients so they can decide whether to wait or retry? e.g. if no new tokens in 300ms we let the client try a fallback.
kevin: Are you talking bytes streamed or semantic tokens? both have different signal shapes.
sasha: token-level if we can, otherwise 'bytes-out' is a fallback. main goal: gate retries to avoid spamming upstream when the model is still churning.
ana: (typo: ana) we could add a trailer header that includes a high-water mark like `x-rw-progress: token_index=1024` so proxies and clients can see forward progress.
ana: code sketch:
```
# trailer example
x-rw-progress: tokens=1024,complete=false
```
matt: Danger: once upstream committed partial output we may have side effects / billing implications. If we retry after partial commit we risk duplication. We need a clear "finality" signal.
kevin: agree. maybe three states: streaming (no finality), committed-partial (persisted/charged), final. Only allow edge-initiated retries in streaming state.
sasha: that's the idea — allow hedging/soft-retries while `complete=false`. once `complete=true` no retries. also include a monotonic token index so we can detect progress vs stagnation.
liz: operational questions: how do we surface this in metrics so SRE can tell if retries are masking slow models? metrics: `edge.progress-p95`, `client-visible-retries`, `hedge-success-rate`.
kevin: also need to account for cost: if we hedge and both upstreams produce output, who gets billed? suggest dedup key on request-id + token-range; gateway only invoices once if it de-dups within a TTL.
matt: that de-duping state needs memory and correctness bounds. TTL 5s maybe ok for short requests, but long streams break that. we should limit hedging to short-window requests (<= 10s).
sasha: proposal for the RFC I'll draft:
- introduce trailer header `x-rw-progress: tokens=NN,complete=(true|false)`
- gateway hedging allowed while complete=false AND token progress delta < threshold for N ms
- default threshold 300ms, configurable per-route
- hedged replicas must set `x-rw-hedge=true` and gateway performs de-dup by request-id with 3s dedup window
- no retry after complete=true (finality)
- tracing: add span `retry.gate` with tags `reason=stall|error` and `hedge=true/false`

ana: backwards compat note: clients that don't understand the trailer should ignore it; avoid breaking semantics.
kevin: rollout plan: feature flag behind `edge.progress-gating` -> 5% canary -> 25% -> 100%. monitor `client-visible-retries` and `errors_after_hedge`.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: feature flag `edge.progress-gating` enabled for canary (5%) at 2024-06-12T14:03:00Z
liz: one more thought—some clients will prefer a keepalive event instead of trailers (websocket / http2 streams). make the API surface consistent: trailers for http1.1+ streaming, keepalives for websockets.
matt: agree. add compatibility matrix in RFC. also call out billing semantics explicitly.
sasha: cool, I'll author RFC draft and ping the architecture reviewers. target: include simple emulation test (simulated slow-token pipeline) + perf numbers.
kevin: :+1: thx.
ana: :shipit:
